Hi Hannah — great to speak earlier. Below is a concise proposal we use for commit-backed pilots; happy to iterate.

Summary (pilot-friendly):
- Pilot length: 3 months.
- Commit option A (monthly): commit to 100M tokens/month; we provide 20% credit (applied as prepaid tokens) in month 1 and a 10% monthly usage credit thereafter if you meet the committed volume.
- Commit option B (quarterly prepaid commit): prepay 300M tokens for the quarter and receive 25% additional pilot credits (one-time).
- Per-token discounts beyond baseline: 100M-299M: 5% off list, 300M-999M: 12% off list, 1B+: custom pricing.
- Minimum contractual term for discounted rates: typically 3 months for pilots, 12 months for annual commits.

We usually include a short mutual action plan:
1) CloudCraft confirms expected average and peak token volumes + success criteria.
2) Redwood issues a short term-sheet with credits and invoicing cadence (Net30 standard; Net60 negotiable with PO).
3) DocuSign PO for the commit and pilot credits applied to your hosted account.

I've attached a one-pager (redwood-commit-summary-v2.pdf) and a short spreadsheet template to capture your monthly projections (cloudcraft-poc-questions.xlsx).

Questions for you now:
- Would you prefer monthly rolling commits or a prepaid quarter?
- Any strict invoice/PO requirements from procurement (Net terms / PO reference format)?

If it's helpful I can block 30 minutes tomorrow to walk through the numbers with procurement + your engineering lead.

Thanks,
